newsitem.title: CHILE: Rio Algom wins Codelco exploration deal.
newsitem.headline: Rio Algom wins Codelco exploration deal.

text.p: Canadian mining company Rio Algom has won a deal with Chile's state copper company Codelco to carry out exploration on a Codelco copper/gold deposit known as Inca de Oro, said Codelco.
The final terms of the contract are still under discussion and it should be signed within the next two-to-three months, a Codelco spokeswoman told Reuters.
"The contract still has to be agreed by the Codelco and Rio Algom boards," she said.
Cyprus and Codelco own the El Abra copper mine which came into production this year.

Codelco is also negotiating with Finnish mining company Outokumpu Oy over prospection on the Mariposa/Cerro Redondo property and with Canada's Cominco Ltd for the Yabricoya site, said the spokeswoman.
Canadian mining company Teck Corp has said it is planning to sign several exploration deals with Codelco, with the first likely to be clinched by the end of the year.
Codelco is keen to carry out deals with private companies to allow them to prospect on deposits which are either too risky, or too small to be of use to the company.
The corporation, which operates four copper pits, owns vast tracts of land in the desert which is at the heart of Chile's booming mining industry.
